messages.text:
Hi Heliumdeploy Team,

I spent a few minutes looking through your website, and the first thing I
noticed was not a design problem.

The brand already has a clear personality. The opportunity is that a
first-time visitor may not understand the full value of the idea as quickly
as someone who already knows the story behind the business.

That matters because buyers rarely study a website patiently. They make
fast decisions about whether a brand feels intentional, trustworthy and
worth exploring.

The issue does not appear to be the products themselves. It is how quickly
the website explains:

* What makes the brand different
* What the products are really for
* Where a new buyer should begin
* Why they should trust the business enough to continue

I can map the first 30 seconds of the buyer journey and show you the three
areas I would strengthen first.

No access or commitment is needed.

Would that outside perspective be useful?

Best regards,
Hassan

Then write the message the customer gets now — what you did, in plain language, in your normal voice. Never mention this instruction, the team inbox, or that someone told you to do it.
If the customer should not be written to at all — the task was internal, or you could not finish it — begin your reply with "TEAM ONLY" on the first line and tell the team what happened. Anything that starts that way stays in the inbox and is never sent.
